Quarterly revenue grew by twelve percent year over year, beating internal forecast and street consensus by a comfortable margin and reaching a new all-time high for the company.
Customer churn dropped to its lowest level in two years across all market segments and product lines, with enterprise retention reaching a record high and mid-market churn down by half.
Three new enterprise accounts signed during the period with multi-year commitments, expanding the named-account roster into two new verticals and unlocking incremental services attach opportunities for next year.
Gross margin expanded by two hundred basis points on improved infrastructure costs, lower third-party data licensing fees, disciplined hosting renegotiations, and a one-time true-up on prior-period accruals.
Product engineering shipped four major feature releases across the platform this quarter, including the long-awaited collaboration suite, the new mobile experience, the analytics rebuild, and a series of small but high-impact ergonomic improvements.
Operating expenses came in below plan despite continued investment in headcount and go-to-market, with disciplined spend management throughout the organization and a deliberate slowing of non-essential travel and consulting engagements.
Sales pipeline coverage exiting the quarter sits comfortably above three times the next-quarter target with a healthier mid-funnel mix than a year ago and a marked increase in deals sourced by the partner channel.
Net dollar retention crossed one hundred and twenty percent for the first time, reflecting both expansion within existing accounts and reduced contraction across the install base, with the largest cohort gains in financial services.
Cash from operations turned solidly positive for the first time in eight quarters, supported by improved collections, more disciplined working capital management, and the timing of certain large customer prepayments.
Hiring plans for the remainder of the year remain on track with offer-accept rates above benchmark and an unusually deep bench of internal candidates progressing toward senior leadership roles in engineering and product.
Customer satisfaction scores set a new high water mark, with both NPS and CSAT measurements showing improvement against the prior quarter and the full prior year on a like-for-like basis.
International expansion progressed in line with the plan, with the EMEA region now contributing roughly one quarter of new logo bookings and APAC pipeline beginning to mature into late-stage opportunities.
